title: The Twelve Greatnesses: The Five-Fold Descent of Divine Truth Reaching Adam
arc: The teaching unfolds the complete cosmology of redemption as a five-fold descent of Divine Greatness — from the hidden Father, through Mother of Life and First Man, through Living Spirit, Third Ambassador, and Jesus the Radiance — until divine truth reaches down even to the molding of Adam and Eve, and from there returns home in the final gathering of all scattered light.
reading:
This chapter is a complete map of how the Lord in his inmost Divine reaches down through discrete degrees into the natural mind of man, and how, having reached it, he draws the captive light home. It is laid out in the form of "Twelve Greatnesses" arranged as five — the standard Manichaean count of completeness in receptive form — with each Greatness naming a distinct station of divine operation. Read correspondentially, this is not a procession of separate gods but the one Lord acting in five successive accommodations, each lower than the last, until the last reaches into Adam's very flesh.

The First Greatness is the Father of Greatness himself, who abides in silence and concealment, established in his own land, in his own substance alone. This is the Divine Esse before any going-forth: love and wisdom in their inmost, hidden state, not yet expressed outward. From him the other four Greatnesses are revealed and "come forth from there," appointed in the midst of glory and standing fast as twelve perfect ones — the twelve being the completeness of every aspect by which the Divine articulates itself outward.

The Second Greatness is the Mother of Life, the Great Spirit, who "gushes forth" beside the First Man with his five sons. Correspondentially this is Divine Wisdom in her bringing-forth: Divine Truth (the First Man) is born from Divine Good through the maternal matrix, and goes down clothed in his five attributes — the five-fold Living Soul that will be dispersed into the natural for redemption. The Third Greatness is the Great Builder, the Living Spirit, with his own five sons: Divine Truth now in its operative, structuring power, the influx that builds order in the receptive natural after the First Man's descent. The Fourth Greatness is the Third Ambassador with the Pillar of Glory and all the powers of light: the awakening Call that exposes captive light and the very column of ascent by which that light returns. The Fifth Greatness is Jesus the Radiance with all his summoned powers and emanations: Divine Truth in its shining-forth as Redeemer, the most accommodated form, the one who actually reaches into the human condition.

The teaching then makes a striking arithmetical move: the twelve "ascendings" are completed by adding two more — the Call and the Answer — which are the Father and the Mother themselves, "in whose likeness Jesus the Radiance" works. The whole cosmic structure of descent, in other words, turns out to be the structure of one Call summoning and one Hearing answering, the influx of Divine Truth and the soul's reception of it, which Jesus embodies as he goes down into the lowest place.

The middle of the teaching dwells on the wrong done to the First Man — Divine Truth descending into the realm of self-love is "sinned against" by the King of Darkness and his archonic associates, who took from him kingship, rank, wealth, and led his being into captivity. He is likened to a noble offspring abased, surrounded by enemies, in the grasp of his foes, and yet "the strong, the standing one." This abasement is the doctrine of the Living Soul: Divine Truth dispersed and bound in the mingled state, the Cross of Light borne in matter. In response, the King of the Lights sends a judge — and this judge, the teaching says outright, is the Living Spirit in his judicial likeness, sent to pass sentence on the violence done to the First Man. He binds the archons in heaven and on earth, measures to each what fits his wickedness, places each in his fitting place — fetters, scourges, crucifixions, sentences of death, dwellings of evil — and sets some over others as powers, so that the falsities work their own corruption out among themselves under the divine restraint. This is the doctrine of the cosmic order of hells: evil is permitted to operate only within bounds the Lord himself has measured.

Then the Third Ambassador comes likewise, "to inspect the works," likened to a great king who walks through his workshops, sees what the craftsmen and architects have made, and either rejoices in their good work or judges the rest. Here the teaching turns to the bitter trees — the corrupt perceptions of the archons — which the Ambassador binds in their own fire so that they cannot put forth shoots from their bodies nor produce bitter fruit for eating: corrupt knowledges are sealed in their own lust so they cannot generate further falsity. After this, the trees of life are planted, which yield good fruits: the new perceptions whose works are good.

The descent then reaches its lowest station in Jesus the Radiance, who in the same likeness comes against this people, expels and binds and afflicts them as fire that burns and destroys corrupt trees. His operation goes through the Zone (the cosmic girdle of states) in many mighty workings until he reaches the molding of the flesh of Adam and Eve — the natural man as fashioned by Saklas-power. Here the teaching reaches its anthropological floor: Divine Truth in its shining-forth descends all the way into the proprium-shaped human, draws his purpose out of Eve, breathes the fragrance of glory into Adam, and ascends. This is the redemption of the human race in its first molded condition: the Lord goes down into the very body of corruption and there plants the seed of return.

The closing movement is the eschatological gathering. The Counsel of Life — the Call together with the Answer — has gone down to the elements that stand fast in agreement, abides there in silence and stillness, and bears the burden upward until the last time. Then he awakens, stands fast in the great fire, gathers his soul to himself, depicts himself in the final destruction (this is the Last Andrias, the consummating gathering-statue), scatters off the defilement that is foreign to him, and gathers all the light scattered through every work back into his own body, where it abides in his image forever. The teaching illustrates this with a beautiful natural figure: a hot stone is dropped into hot milk, drawing the milk to itself, ripening it, until the milk's sweetness and oil and beauty are gathered into the stone — and the bonds of falsity around the soul fall away. So the Counsel of Life, planted in the elements, ripens the dispersed light by its own heat and at last takes the whole sweetness home.

Read as one argument, the teaching describes the complete arc of correspondence between heaven and earth: the Father in concealment → the Mother bringing forth Divine Truth → the Living Spirit building structure and judging the archons → the Ambassador inspecting and sealing the corrupt perceptions → Jesus the Radiance reaching the molded flesh of Adam — and then the long return, in which the soul awakens, stands, gathers, and brings every grain of scattered light home in the image of its sender. The whole drama is the doctrine that the Lord descends to the lowest in order to carry the lowest back up, and that the same five-fold structure that organizes his coming organizes his returning.
